# Lab 23.1: Data Protection Building Blocks

## What We Are Going to Do
Review the built-in protections (time travel, fail-safe, snapshots), then automate daily snapshot backups with a scheduled script.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Create the dataset and a table to protect.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq --location=US mk --dataset $PROJECT_ID:lab23
bq --location=US mk --dataset --default_table_expiration=2592000 $PROJECT_ID:lab23_backups
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'CREATE TABLE lab23.orders AS SELECT * FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders`'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Tables in `lab23_backups` expire after 30 days automatically.

2. **Review the layers.**

   | Layer | Covers | Kept for |
   |---|---|---|
   | Time travel | Any change or delete | 2–7 days |
   | Fail-safe | Deleted data, via support | 7 more days |
   | Snapshots | A point in time you choose | Until expiry |
   | Cross-region replica | Region outage | Continuous |

3. **[SQL] Write the backup script.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">DECLARE snap_name STRING DEFAULT FORMAT('lab23_backups.orders_%s', FORMAT_DATE('%Y%m%d', CURRENT_DATE()));
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE FORMAT('CREATE SNAPSHOT TABLE IF NOT EXISTS %s CLONE lab23.orders', snap_name);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Schedule it.** Click **Schedule → Create new scheduled query**, name `daily_orders_snapshot`, daily at 01:00. Don't set a destination table (the script creates it).

5. **[CLI] Test a restore.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq ls lab23_backups
SNAP=$(bq ls --format=json lab23_backups | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)[-1]['tableReference']['tableId'])")
bq cp --restore -f lab23_backups.$SNAP lab23.orders_restored
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM lab23.orders_restored'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Time travel + fail-safe | Short-term recovery, built in |
| Snapshots | Long-term, cheap backups |
| Automation | Daily scheduled script |
| Restore | `bq cp --restore` |
